event_confirmation: Company press release via GlobeNewswire, datelined NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026: 'Cipher Digital Announces Date of Third Quarter 2026 Business Update Conference Call' - results before U.S. markets open on Monday, November 2nd, 2026, call at 8:00 a.m. ET. https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/21/tmt-newswire/globenewswire/cipher-digital-announces-date-of-third-quarter-2026-business-update-conference-call/2450226 (also https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/cipher-digital-announces-date-third-quarter-2026-business-update-conference-call-2026). Session bmo confirmed.
conviction_note: The event is real (company release of 20 Oct, bmo 2 Nov). The stock is down 53.6% in 20 days to a 52-week low. That drawdown has documented causes: an $850m zero-coupon convert plus a 40.7m-share exchange, a Barber Lake delivery slip with a $359m cost overrun borne by Cipher, and a sector-wide AI-infrastructure selloff. Short interest is about 22% of float and the option skew is call-bid at -14.7 vol points. Against that sit a positive optionality (the company has paired prints with lease announcements, AWS on the Q3 2025 print at +20%; 477 MW is available for 2027) and a 'first rent in Q4' confirmation the market is waiting for. The negatives are a Google-warrant $430m value floor that crystallises at Barber Lake commencement and the risk of another slip. Findings sum to +2.1. The scaled number is (2x0.55-1)x17 = +1.7: the lean is mostly proxies, inference and positioning, not an unseen company number, so p_up sits only slightly above 50.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus: EPS -$0.2358 and revenue $38.44m, from one aggregator article dated 2026-10-26 (https://moneycheck.com/?p=188317). There is no company guide (the Q2 release gave no Q3 numbers: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819989/000181998926000038/q226_earningsxprxdraftxvf.htm) and no second estimate source was found, so the bar is single-source and any finding that depends on beat/miss is capped small. Q2 printed revenue of $24.84m against $31.86m expected and EPS of -$0.65 against -$0.25. The stock trades on HPC lease delivery, rent timing and new leases, not on the reported quarter's revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest is 21.7% of float as of the 2026-09-30 settlement, with 1.7 days to cover (Tapeboard, a third-party aggregator, not FINRA direct: https://tapeboard.com/stock/CIFR, and the daily most-shorted boards of 2026-10-14/19/20 at https://tapeboard.com/most-shorted-stocks/2026-10-20). Earlier readings: 65.5m shares short at the 2026-08-14 settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cifr/short-interest/). Convert-arb hedging after the 14 Oct pricing of the $850m 2032 notes plausibly added short, unmeasured. Baseline: skew_25d -14.74 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.47, ATM IV 157.8%, event-implied move 15.86%, run-up -53.63% over 20d and -8.25% over 5d, at the 52-week low (-75% from the high). This is a crowded, washed-out short with the option market leaning up.

findings.finding: Barber Lake rent start is the line the market is waiting on. The 25 Sep amendment moved hall deliveries from 'September 2026' (Q2 10-Q) to phased Q4 2026-Q1 2027, with first rent expected in Q4 2026. The 13 Oct offering deck (Ex. 99.1) dates Halls 1-2 to Q4 2026, Halls 3-4 to Q4 2026-Q1 2027 and Hall 5 to Q1 2027, and states 'no rent credits incurred to date'. A 2 Nov confirmation that Halls 1-2 were delivered or rent commenced (which commentary expected in October) removes the main execution fear; a second slip would hit a stock already -53% in 20 days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 25 Sep slip-plus-extension release was sold, about -3% that day (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/30/cipher-digital-slips-3-despite-20-year-barber-lake-lease-extension-terawulf-retreats-2-iren-limited-treads-water/). The early Black Pearl delivery on the Q2 print (4 Aug) did not save it: -15.65% on the revenue miss. The early AWS-lease print (Q3 2025) rallied about +20%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock at a 52-week low, a $3.3bn market cap against more than $9bn of Barber Lake contracted revenue, and press framing around 'stranded capacity' (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/ai-infrastructure-stocks-rise-as-rebound-from-steep-selloff-extends-cipher-digital-jumps-8-iren-climbs-7-terawulf-gains-5/) all say the market prices meaningful risk of further slippage. If it were priced as on track, the stock would not have fallen from $13.5 to $7.3 after the deck that restated the schedule.
findings.independence: The Sep 25 8-K press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000181998926000043/barberlakeleaseamendmentpr.htm) says the company 'remains on track with the revised delivery schedule'. Same issuer, a different document, and earlier. No third-party confirmation of hall delivery was found.

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded and washed out into the print. Short interest is about 21.7% of float (30 Sep) before convert-arb hedging of the 14 Oct $850m notes; the stock is -53.6% over 20 days and at its 52-week low; the 25-delta skew is -14.7 vol points (calls over puts) with put/call OI 0.47. Any non-negative print has a squeeze mechanism, as the +8% sector bounce on 27 Oct showed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline reactions: -15.65% (Aug 2026), +23.53% (May 2026), +12.48% (Feb 2026); two of three up. The 27 Oct sector bounce took CIFR +8% at the open, the most of its peer group.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the call-bid skew already says the option market expects upside. What is not in the price is the size of a short-cover on a ~22%-short name if Barber Lake rent is confirmed. If shorts expected a further leg down they would be paying for puts, not leaving calls bid.
findings.independence: Baseline skew (-14.74) and P/C OI 0.47 come from the sealed Yahoo options data, a different source from Tapeboard. Curvedtrading's August reading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cifr/short-interest/) shows short interest was already high.

findings.finding: The company has paired quarterly prints with major lease announcements: the Q3 2025 print (3 Nov 2025) came with the $5.5bn 15-year AWS lease and the Colchis 1 GW JV, and the stock rose about 20% that day. Cipher now says 477 MW (Odessa, Reveille, Ulysses) could be available in 2027 outside ERCOT batch study, with no Odessa lease announced as of 9 Oct, Colchis holding conditional Batch Zero status and Apollo submitted. A signed lease on 2 Nov is a real but unannounced possibility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 print plus AWS lease: opened about -2%, closed up about 20-22% (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/11/03/why-cipher-mining-stock-soared-on-monday-morning/). May 2026 print: +23.53% (baseline). The 25 Sep 2026 lease extension: -3% (sold).
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only: no document says a lease is imminent. A stock at a 52-week low with a $18 low target (range $18-59) prices little probability of a new lease. If a lease were expected, the stock would have been bid into the print rather than falling 5% on 29 Oct ahead of earnings.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 precedent (https://www.theblock.co/post/377285/cipher-mining-shares-jump-5-5-billion-usd-aws-ai-deal-1gw-texas-site) and the 13 Oct deck's 3.4 GW pipeline with Colchis and Apollo (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000119312526419743/d134900dex991.htm). This is a proxy/pattern, not a dated catalyst.

findings.finding: The Google warrants (24,178,576 shares at $0.01) carry a $430.0m value floor ('shortfall provision'): if the warrant shares are worth less than $430m on the business day before the exercise period starts, which is Barber Lake lease commencement, Cipher must issue more shares or pay cash. At the $7.285 spot the shares are worth about $176m, implying a shortfall of about $254m, roughly 35m more shares (about 8% dilution) or $254m of cash. Commencement is guided for Q4 2026, so the Q3 10-Q or the call will put it in front of investors.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line. The nearest analogue is the 14 Oct convert plus 40.7m-share exchange, which took the stock -25.7% over the week (https://www.fool.com/coverage/market-movers/2026/10/16/why-cipher-digital-stock-plunged-26-this-week/), though that also carried the sector CPI selloff.
findings.why_not_priced: The provision is in the 10-Q, but nothing in the October coverage (TIKR, Fool, 24/7) quantifies it at today's price. It mattered little at $24.50 (shares worth $592m against a $430m floor) and only bites after the 53% fall. If it were priced, previews would list warrant dilution beside the convert dilution.
findings.independence: Same document family. The warrant-share count is corroborated by the EPS note of the same 10-Q. No outside source has quantified the shortfall. The financing question was asked: this obligation buys nothing new (it is a fixed contractual make-whole), so it is negative. It is shrunk for the crowded short and because the company can settle part in cash from the convert proceeds.

findings.finding: The Q3 GAAP line will carry a large non-cash gain on the warrant liability. It stood at $632.1m at 30 Jun with the stock at $24.50 and produced a $150.5m Q2 loss that drove the -$0.65 EPS miss. With the stock near $16 at 30 Sep and the $430m floor, the liability should fall by roughly $180-200m, about +$0.45/share. Headline GAAP EPS should therefore print well above the -$0.24 consensus, possibly positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the warrant loss turned EPS into a -$0.65 miss and the stock fell -15.65%, but revenue also missed by 22%, so the line's own effect cannot be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Single-source consensus of -$0.2358 looks like it excludes the remeasurement. Only a headline-algo effect is unpriced, since informed holders see through non-cash warrant marks. Sized as a one-off with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: The 30 Sep price level is inferred from a $14.56 close on 7 Oct and $18.10 on 24 Sep (Yahoo snippets via search); the $430m floor comes from the 10-Q Note 16. This shares the 10-Q with the shortfall finding, but the two are different periods and different effects (Q3 P&L gain against Q4 settlement), so both stand.

findings.finding: Financing done before the print: $850m of 0% 2032 converts (conversion $15.31, capped call to $28.35) closed 16 Oct, $165.9m of 2030 notes were exchanged for 40.7m shares (about 10% dilution, already issued), and the default settlement of the 2030 and 2031 notes was switched to physical (shares). Proceeds fund about $750m of extra Barber Lake project equity and the HPC pipeline. The deck says Barber Lake needs $187-200m more to complete, which is rentalized for $480m of extra revenue. Whether the $150m greenshoe (13-day option from 16 Oct) was exercised is not yet disclosed and should appear in the Q3 10-Q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The offering week was -25.7%. The June $810m debt deal was -7.75% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: This is fully priced (the -26% week). It is filed because the question 'what does the money buy' has an answer: it funds Barber Lake completion against contracted, Google-backstopped rent. That makes it a zero, not a further negative. A greenshoe exercise or non-exercise is a small signal of convert demand.
findings.independence: The 13 Oct 8-K/press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000119312526419743/d134900dex992.htm) states the use of proceeds; TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/cipher-digital-slides-30-after-zero-coupon-note-sale-despite-9-billion-barber-lake-backlog) reports the dilution.

findings.finding: Sector tape into the window is fragile. Alphabet, the Fluidstack backstop and warrant holder, reported $51.3bn of quarterly capex and -$9.1bn FCF, and AI-infrastructure names fell (IREN -6%, CIFR -5% to about -11%) on 29 Oct. Higher hyperscaler capex is demand for Cipher's capacity, but the market is reading it as credit risk for neoclouds and ex-miners.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CIFR is the largest WGMI holding and trades as a high-beta member of the AI-infra group: -12.35% on the 14 Oct CPI selloff (https://cointelegraph.com/markets/bitcoin-miners-plunge-up-to-13-in-wall-streets-worst-selloff-since-july), +8% on the 27 Oct bounce.
findings.why_not_priced: This is priced before entry. It is filed because it sets the beta the print lands on: an idiosyncratic beat can be swamped by the group's direction on 2 Nov. It is a sector proxy, sized 0.
findings.independence: The Benzinga piece on neocloud credit risk (https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/10/62578790/riot-mara-iren-and-corz-stocks-slide-as-bitcoin-miners-turn-neoclouds-face-credit-risks), 403 on fetch, title only.

outside_window.finding: Settlement of the Google-warrant $430m shortfall itself, in cash or additional shares, occurs at Barber Lake lease commencement (Q4 2026, likely after 2 Nov). Only its disclosure falls in the window, and that is filed above; the actual issuance or cash outflow comes later.
Odessa power contract runs through end of July 2027; first 2027 megawatts there depend on signing a lease. If no lease comes on the print, the decision is deferred.

Analyst preview or downgrade in the last week of October: none found. Only Cantor's PT cut to $19 (16 Oct) and Morgan Stanley's to $51.50 (9 Oct), both priced.
8-K after 16 Oct (greenshoe exercise, new lease): none on EDGAR as of 30 Oct.
Exact 30 Sep 2026 closing price: not found; inferred from the 24 Sep ($18.10) and 7 Oct ($14.56) closes.

rejected_candidates.candidate: 13 Oct deck line read as 'Black Pearl lease amended to add 10 years with a leading AI lab'
rejected_candidates.detail: Extracted from slide images. The Q2 10-Q shows the Black Pearl tenant as an investment-grade hyperscaler (AWS), and the $16.6bn contracted total (+46% vs Q2) reconciles to the Barber Lake +$5.2bn alone, so this is almost certainly an OCR conflation with the Barber Lake AI-lab commitment. Not filed as a separate finding.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q3 revenue vs $38.44m consensus: Black Pearl rent from early August plus a stronger Q3 hashprice (Luxor Sept average ~$39.33/PH/day) against reduced mining capacity after decommissioning
rejected_candidates.detail: No sourced MW or rent figure for Black Pearl's first tranche exists, so this cannot be sized beyond the single-source bar. It is folded into print_vs_bar_pct = 0 rather than filed as its own finding.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the call-bid skew (-14.7) and cut against the -53.6% 20-day run-up only in the sense that the run-up has documented causes now in the price. The lean is mildly positive and mostly from positioning and optionality, so p_up is held at 55, close to 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): the Barber Lake rent finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8 for the slip risk written in its own text.
Lesson 5/7 (positioning is the thing to beat, not a cause by itself): the positioning finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, since part of it is already in the call-bid skew.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): the warrant-shortfall negative cut from -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the warrant-remeasurement GAAP gain cut from +0.5 to +0.3, with no path to the guide.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the convert/exchange stays at 0 after asking what it buys (Barber Lake completion against backstopped rent).
Lesson 6 (single-source bar): print_vs_bar held at 0 and no finding sized on revenue beat/miss; p_up moved 56 -> 55.
